claims.claim: Severian of Gabala was Bishop of Gabala in Syria.
Severian flourished in the fourth and fifth centuries and died after 408.
Severian was a popular preacher in Constantinople from around 400 until 404.
Severian became the enemy of John Chrysostom and helped condemn him at the Synod of the Oak.
In Greek, almost all of Severian's homilies survive only among the works of his enemy Chrysostom.
The work is catalogued as CPG 4236.2 in the Clavis Patrum Graecorum.
The incipit of the homily is Χθὲς ἡμῖν, ἀδελφοί, ὁ περὶ.
The homily was previously listed under CPG 4761 before being reattributed to Severian.
More than 50 of Severian's sermons are extant.
Almost none of Severian's works have been edited critically, and some have never been published.
